verses.note: The first thing Scripture calls holy is a day. Holiness here means belonging to God in a special way, and time is claimed before any place or person is. Israel's sacred calendar, and later the Christian Lord's Day, grow from this root.

Joseph's reasons begin with loyalty to Potiphar but end with God. A sin against a neighbor is first a sin against God, which is how David will later confess his adultery (Psalm 51:4). Holiness here is not ritual separation but faithfulness in a private room with no one watching.

Holiness here is not a property of the soil but of God's presence, which makes an ordinary hillside a place to be approached with reverence and limits. The verse teaches that God's nearness and God's otherness come together: he calls Moses close and tells him how close he may come.

The people cannot stay close to the place where God speaks. Their distance is not simply fear but a right perception of the gulf between the holy God and sinful people, which the following verses address with a mediator.

Holiness here means keeping human craft and human exposure away from the place where God meets his people. The altar is to be something God gives rather than something humans display their skill in, and worship is to be free of the sexual display that marked some neighboring cults.
After the calf, the approach to God is narrowed to one mediator. The people's sin has made the distance greater than before, and even their animals are kept away from the holy mountain.

Even the high priest, on the appointed day, in the right clothing, cannot look on the place of God's presence. The incense cloud screens him from a sight that would kill him, as Moses was hidden in the rock when God's glory passed (Exodus 33:20-22).

The things that carried impurity away also pass impurity to those who handle them, so the men who serve in the rite must wash before returning. The same paradox appears with the ashes of the red heifer (Numbers 19:7-10): what cleanses the community leaves those who administer it needing cleansing.
